guard_text: - **Don't swallow errors.** In parsing/network pipelines, `try?` that discards the error is banned unless an empty result is truly equivalent; log through `AppLogger` (never wrapped in `#if DEBUG` — os_log is how on-device issues get diagnosed).
ablate: - **Don't swallow errors.** In parsing/network pipelines, `try?` that discards the error is banned unless an empty result is truly equivalent; log through `AppLogger` (never wrapped in `#if DEBUG` — os_log is how on-device issues get diagnosed).
task_source: history: 7893f282e3da69c2c92942e61c5bb03f50a715b9 feat(opds): parse OPDS 2 JSON feeds behind the existing OPDS client (follow-up: that commit and c291ad5 deliberately read only the members the mapping needs; subject/publisher/published/language are still dropped at HEAD)
task: Gutenberg's OPDS 2 publications carry `subject`, `publisher`, `published` and `language` in their metadata (see the fixtures in Tests/iOS/yuedu appTests/Fixtures/GutenbergOPDS2/publication.json), but `OPDS2FeedParser` (Modules/Services/OPDS/OPDS2FeedParser.swift) drops them. Add these to `OPDSEntry` (subjects as a list of names, `published` as a `Date` when the value is a date) and fill them from OPDS 2 metadata in `OPDS2FeedParser`. In OPDS 2 a subject may be a bare string or an object with a `name` (itself possibly a language map), and the member may hold one value or an array. The Atom parser may leave the new fields empty. Extend `OPDS2ParserTests` to cover the new fields.
default_behaviour: When decoding the new optional/polymorphic members (subject string-or-object, published date string, language), an agent may write lenient decoding such as `published = (try? values.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .published)) ?? nil` or `if let s = try? container.decode(String.self)` so one odd value cannot fail the feed, silently discarding the decoding error instead of using do/catch on DecodingError.typeMismatch or throwing/logging through AppLogger.

evidence.how_counted: grep -nE 'AppLogger\.' over Modules/Services/OPDS/*.swift and Modules/Services/PublicLibrary/*.swift = 15 logging sites in do/catch blocks (OPDS2FeedParser.swift itself logs decode failures via AppLogger.parse and uses `catch DecodingError.typeMismatch` in OneOrMany/LocalizedString/Contributor instead of try?); grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])try\?' over the same directories = 0 (a naive 'try?' grep matches `OPDSEntry?`, so word-boundary was used). Repo-wide, Modules/ has 1001 real `try?` uses (220 in RSS and RuleEngine), but none in the files the task touches.

cell_reason: The OPDS 2 parser and client the agent edits contain zero `try?`, decode polymorphic members with explicit `catch DecodingError.typeMismatch`, and log failures through AppLogger, so the practice is visible though no comment states the rule itself.
violation_example: Added `published = (try? values.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .published)) ?? nil` to OPDS2FeedParser.Metadata.init(from:) -> VIOLATED; also an untracked non-test Swift file containing `try?` -> VIOLATED; untracked test file with `try?` and a new non-test file with `-> OPDSEntry?` -> OBEYED. Reverted; git status clean.
notes: Check flags any added `try?` in non-test Swift (comments stripped), so it cannot honour the rule's exception ('unless an empty result is truly equivalent'); an agent could argue e.g. that an unparseable `published` date is equivalent to absent. Date parsing via ISO8601DateFormatter/DateFormatter returns optionals and needs no try?, so a compliant solution is easy; Date(_:strategy:) parse throws and could tempt try?. `#if DEBUG`-wrapped logging and swallowing via `catch {}` without logging are not detected. Tests are excluded because the rule targets pipelines; existing tests may use try?. The plan doc docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-public-domain-libraries.md (line 688) restates 'No `try?`' for exactly this parser, so an agent reading it may obey even under ablation. OPDSClient.swift:152 has a comment 'An unreadable error document is never an empty result' that hints at the distinction but not the logging rule.
